evaluationCost.note: evaluation cost; never added to arm cost

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new due-date rule (`NetEndOfMonth` in `Invoicing.dueDate`) is in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The terms text is also produced there. The parsing and validation of the form value is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2) and the stored record format is in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). Tier 3 and Tier 4 code is not touched, so nothing is re-decided above Tier 2.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no clock, randomness, I/O or console access. `dueDate` is pure and takes the issue date as an argument. The parser is pure string and integer handling. The storage encoding is pure JSON construction.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The wording 'Net N EOM' is written in two places, `Documents.termsText` and the private `Invoicing.termsWords`. The existing `Net` case already has the same split, so the change follows the existing pattern. The two copies agree, but they could drift. The 1 to 365 day bound is copied from the existing `Net` branch of the parser inside the same function. The two bounds agree. The due-date rule and the storage kind `net-eom` each have a single definition.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The `DayOfNextMonth` due-date rule is in `Invoicing.dueDate` (Ledger, Tier 1). The ordinal helper is also in Ledger. The `day N` parsing and the 1 to 28 validation are in the engine (Tier 2), and the storage codec is in Storage (Tier 2). Tier 3 and Tier 4 code is not touched.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effects are added. `dueDate` uses `DateOnly` arithmetic on its arguments only. The `ordinal` function, the parser and the codec are all pure.

evidence.quote: | DayOfNextMonth day -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"
| Some(DayOfNextMonth day) -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The ordinal logic is defined once (`Invoicing.ordinal`) and both sites call it, which is good. The phrase 'Due the Nth of next month' is still written in both `termsText` and `termsWords`, as in change set 1. The copies agree. The 1 to 28 bound appears only in the engine parser and the stored value is not re-validated. That is consistent with how `Net` is handled, and it is not a second definition.
